title: Two Piles as Equal as Possible

concept.title: Track the difference, and cut a branch when the best end is known
body: Put each of `n` numbers into pile A or pile B so that the sums differ as little as possible. Track only the **difference** `diff = sum(A) - sum(B)`: a number added to A raises it, a number added to B lowers it. At the end the answer for this choice is `|diff|`.

A strong pruning idea: look at `rest`, the sum of the numbers not yet placed. If `|diff|` is already at least `rest`, then the best possible ending is to put **all** remaining numbers on the lighter side, which gives exactly `|diff| - rest`. There is nothing left to try, so return it at once.
Handling the **big numbers first** makes this prune much more often, because the remaining sum drops fast, so the numbers are sorted in decreasing order.

statement: Given `n` positive integers, split them into two piles (every number goes to exactly one pile; a pile may be empty) so that the difference between the sums of the two piles is as small as possible. Print this smallest difference.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` integers.

examples.note: The piles 8 + 5 = 13 and 6 + 7 = 13 have the same sum, so the difference is 0.

hints: Track sum(A) - sum(B): adding to A raises it, adding to B lowers it.
At the end the answer of a choice is the absolute value of the difference.
If the difference is at least the sum of the numbers still to place, put them all on the lighter pile and stop.

solution.complexity: Time O(2^n) in the worst case, usually much less; space O(n).
